Hi Samantha / Alan —

Thanks again for a productive demo today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we all have the same next steps. Main constraints you emphasized: all PHI in transcripts and embeddings, BAA required, SOC 2 evidence required for procurement, and audit log retention of 7 years for certain clinical records.

Summary of discussion (high level):
- Use case: real-time assistant + nightly batch embedding index for clinical notes (PHI).
- Traffic profile: ~100 concurrent users at peak, ~25k tokens/day initially, expected to grow 3–4x in 12 months.
- Compliance asks: BAA, SOC 2 Type II report, encryption at rest + in transit, customer-managed keys preferred, audit logs and retention policy, and support for penetration test evidence if required.

Deployment modes we covered on the call: Hosted API (with BAA), Dedicated reserved capacity (customer-isolated GPU pool), Private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem install). You asked for a recommendation and the specific evidence we can provide for procurement.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Can Redwood sign a BAA?
2) Please share our SOC 2 report and the sections that speak to logging, access controls, and key management.
3) Rough timelines and prerequisites for Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem).
4) Sample network topology and what level of network isolation is possible.

Attached: redwood-SOC2-report-2025.pdf (SOC 2), draft-BAA-MedicalTech.docx (BAA template we can start from), deployment-topology-diagram.png (example).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in our Solutions and Procurement leads to answer the technical/timing and contract questions (cc’d).
- If you can share a short compliance checklist or procurement contact, we’ll prioritize the items and send a single packet for review.

Would you be available for a 30-minute follow-up on Wed Mar 4 to walk procurement and security through the packet?

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Deployment options & evidence requested (MedicalTech) — technical rundown + timeline

Hi all — thanks for the clear ask list. Below are concise answers and recommended next steps. I’ve attached redwood-SOC2-report-2025.pdf and draft-BAA-MedicalTech.docx again in case procurement needs the originals, plus a high-level deployment-topology-diagram.png.

Short answers:
- BAA: Redwood executes a BAA for customers handling PHI. We can start from the draft you received; legal will want to review a few clauses but execution is standard.
- SOC 2: We can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report (2025) under an NDA / secure link. The sections relevant to your asks are: CC6 (Access Controls), CC7 (System Operations), and CC8 (Change Management). We also include sampling of audit logs (redaction available).
- KMS / keys: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS with BYOK flows; for Dedicated and Private on cloud we can integrate with your KMS/HSM. For on-prem we can configure local HSMs and a customer-managed key policy.
- Network isolation: Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering provides private network paths and no public ingress to the inference nodes. Private (on-prem) is fully isolated but requires additional networking setup and runbook review.

Provisioning timelines (approx):
- Hosted API + BAA: immediate (1–3 business days for contract); production-ready in hours but note that Hosted routes may be less desirable for PHI despite a signed BAA.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) + VPC peering: typically 2–4 weeks (depends on peering approvals, firewall rules, and quota).
- Private VPC / on-prem appliance: 4–8 weeks (legal + network + ops integration; on-prem adds hardware lead times).

Audit logs & retention:
- We store request-level audit logs (request id, user id, model used, tokens, timestamp) and can retain per-customer logs for configurable periods; default long-term archival is available via S3 export (customers can keep archives for 7+ years if needed). We can provide sample log extracts in CSV/JSON for your audit team.

Recommended path based on your timeline (Mar 15 security review):
1) Prioritize Dedicated reserved capacity with VPC peering and a signed BAA — this hits most requirements and can be provisioned within your review window if we start immediately.
2) In parallel, execute the BAA and prepare SOC 2 deliverables (we’ll provide an NDA/secure link to the full report).
3) If you still require on-prem later, treat that as a migration plan after initial onboarding.

Action items for MedicalTech (please confirm):
- Provide a short workload profile (avg RPS, token distribution, any long audio/video payloads).
- Procurement contact (procurement@medicaltech.com confirmed by Samantha).
- Security contact for KMS/HSM integration (Alan, tagging you here).

I’ll prepare a 2-slide summary for Wed’s call covering: evidence we’ll provide, timeline, and the recommended path.

Regards,
